headline: Japan's state-backed chipmaker Rapidus, which has $15 billion in government support, still needs customers as it prepares to make the most advanced chips next year.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: Reuters analysis with outside experts, no new deal.
importance_line: Success would give chip buyers a fourth maker of the most advanced chips and help Japan's industry, but Rapidus has no manufacturing record and analysts say commercial success is far from guaranteed.
summary: Reuters reports in an analysis that Rapidus, Japan's state-backed chipmaker set up in 2022, plans to start making 2-nanometre chips, the most advanced class, in the second half of the next fiscal year, but still needs customers; on Monday it said it would partner with 17 firms, including Synopsys and Infosys, to help clients design chips. An analyst quoted says that announcement is not evidence of commercial traction and that running a fab with stable yields is extremely difficult, and Rapidus has so far received $15 billion in government support.
notes: Read the Reuters text on wincountry.com (WNWN-FM), a copy site; original Reuters link not found. Reuters credited inside the text.
